Title: Real provider opt-in and malformed response
Test Case Description: [Stage 1 target] Verify explicit environment-only real mode; transport security; strict normalization; and safe malformed/upstream failures
Pre-Conditions:
1. Fake mode is default and real provider is never contacted without explicit mode
2. Local test sentinel is available for real malformed/non-2xx responses; live provider is prohibited
3. Environment values are synthetic and isolated
4. Controller, manager, provider logs/traces, and response correlation are observable
Test Steps:
1. Confirm absent opt-in uses fake mode and sentinel has zero hits
2. Add any `sr_code` or `password` query parameter, including to a POST with a valid credential body, and submit malformed body input; assert 422 rejection before provider invocation
3. Enable only ACADEMIC_PROVIDER_MODE; ACADEMIC_PROVIDER_BASE_URL; ACADEMIC_PROVIDER_KEY; ACADEMIC_PROVIDER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2; and ACADEMIC_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5 as applicable
4. Verify missing real configuration fails closed
5. Verify non-HTTPS real base URLs are rejected, except an explicit 127.0.0.1/::1/localhost sentinel when APP_ENV is local/testing
6. Verify cURL TLS peer and host verification are enabled
7. Send malformed, forbidden-field/token/password/raw-PII, and upstream non-2xx responses from the local sentinel, never live provider; for each malformed, forbidden-field, and non-2xx scenario, record the starting hit count, require exactly one additional sentinel hit, and require respectively `503 academic_provider_malformed`, `503 academic_provider_malformed`, and `503 academic_provider_unavailable` (a pre-transport configuration failure does not satisfy the case)
8. Inspect status, strict normalized schema parity with fake, raw-body absence, correlation_id propagation, and logs/traces
Expected Result:
1. [Stage 1 target] Missing real configuration returns HTTP 503 and never calls live provider
2. The malformed sentinel response produces exactly one additional sentinel hit and returns HTTP 503 code `academic_provider_malformed`; the forbidden-field sentinel response likewise produces exactly one additional hit and returns HTTP 503 code `academic_provider_malformed`; the non-2xx sentinel response produces exactly one additional hit and returns HTTP 503 code `academic_provider_unavailable` (pre-transport configuration failure does not satisfy any scenario)
3. Non-HTTPS real URLs fail closed; only explicit loopback sentinel URLs are allowed under APP_ENV local/testing
4. cURL TLS peer and host verification remain enabled
5. Real success uses exactly the fake provider's strict whitelist schema; arbitrary forbidden fields/tokens/passwords/raw PII are rejected or omitted
6. Raw provider payload is absent; credentials, key, token, password, and PII never appear in response/logs/traces
7. One correlation_id is identical across controller/manager/provider logs/traces and response
8. Every unexpected failure has a structured ERROR with exception class, message-safe category, stack, cause, and correlation_id; invalid credentials may be WARN/INFO only
9. Real credentials are environment-only and never sourced from or returned by the request
